texts.preamble: Shri Govind Das Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 May, 2022 Author: Rajendra Kumar Verma Bench: Rajendra Kumar Verma 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pra At Indore Crr No. 1677 of (Shri Govind Das Gupta Vs The Dated : 10-05-2022
texts.facts: Heard on I.A.No.6401/2022, which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant. The applicant has been convicted for offence under Sections 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo 6 months R.I. with fine of Rs.6,000/- with default stipulation.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime. He further submits that the sample was taken from the lot which was not kept for sale in the shop, rather it was kept by the applicant in his house for disposal. The entire prosecution case is based on the testimony of B.S.Solanki (PW-1), the Food Inspector. Nothing is stated regarding the mandatory compliance of provisions of Section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954. As per the statement of Dilip Kumar (PW-3), notice under Section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act was sent to the applicant on 16.02.2009, but acknowledgment Ex.P-25 is dated 14.02.2009, so SAN REENA JOSEPH Date: 2022.05.10 it is not possible that the notice dated 16.02.2009 was received by the applicant, 18:04:38 IST as the acknowledgment receipt depicts the date as 14.02.2009. It is also submitted that (DW-1), the applicant categorically stated in his statement that packets were kept in the Almirah of the house and the Food Inspector searched the house and there is no denial of this statement. It is also submitted that the applicant is aged about 82 years. There is no possibility of early hearing of this revision. Under these circumstances, counsel Shri Govind Das Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54140383/ 1 prays for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to the applicant. Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State o n t h e other hand, has opposed the bail application by submitting that no sufficient ground is made out for releasing the applicant on bail, hence the application filed by the applicant be dismissed.
